items.title: fix(mcpx): scope gopls-mcp-server to the worktree (#961)
items.body: Closes #961. ## Summary - Flip `gopls-mcp-server` to `"scope": "worktree"` in `.mcpx.json`, now that its dependencies have landed: #958 (PR #3925, `ResolvedScope` plumbing + spawn cwd) and #959 (initialize `rootUri`/`workspaceFolders`). - This is the deliberate last slice named in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0004-scope-resolved-roots.md` ("the config flip is deliberately the last slice"). ## On #864 (absolute paths) #864 covers the `codedb` and `fff` entries, which carry `/home/user/...` paths. The `gopls-mcp-server` entry has no absolute paths (`go run golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest mcp`), so the post-#864 config shape does not block this flip, and the flip does not pre-empt #864. ## Verification - `.mcpx.json` parses; `gopls-mcp-server` resolves to `{command, args, mcpx:{scope:"worktree"}}`. - `cd pkgs/mcpx && go test ./internal/config/ -run 'Scope|Extras|Parse' -count=1` → ok. ## Remaining acceptance (live proof, owed) This PR lands the config flip. The live proof from #961 still needs a machine with a running mcpx daemon and Go toolchain, and is being tracked by the queue task rather than asserted here: 1. `go_package_api` on a module path returns the real API promptly (not empty), 2. the same proof from a linked worktree is rooted in that worktree, 3. two callers in different checkouts show distinct gopls instances in `mcpx status`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: mcpx: ResolvedScope plumbing + spawn cwd = resolved scope root (#958)
items.body: Closes #958 — slice 1 of decision record 0004 (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0004-scope-resolved-roots.md`), sections 1/2/3/6. ## What changed - **`internal/config`** — `ResolvedScope{Key, Root, Degraded}` + `Scope.Resolve(ctx)`; `Scope.Key` is now `Resolve(ctx).Key` (one resolution path). Root semantics per §1: worktree → checkout top-level; repo → parent of the common dir only when its base is `.git`, else none; cwd → canonical caller cwd; degraded repo/worktree → that cwd; global/session/psession/pid/call → none. - **Plumbing (§2)** — the registry resolves via `Resolve` (`resolvedFor`) and passes the `ResolvedScope` into `Pool.Acquire`/`Call`/`ReadResource`/`GetPrompt`/`Request`/`Complete`/`Watch`. The pool stores `root` on the `Instance` at creation; `startLane`/`dial` read it from the instance — restarts, era redials, exec-watch replacements and handoffs keep the creation root and never re-resolve. - **Spawn cwd (§3)** — `pool.SpawnCwd`, a pure function: config cwd → resolved root → unset (daemon cwd), applied to both stdio and supervised transports. - **Observability (§6)** — one `server.spawn` lifecycle line per spawn (server, key, root, cwd, cwd source: `config`/`scope`/`daemon`); `key`/`root`/`cwdSource` also on `server.start`; `root` in `mcpx status` instance JSON. ## Tests - New: `Resolve` root semantics (worktree, repo from subdir, repo from a linked worktree roots at the main worktree, cwd, degraded-to-cwd root, rootless scopes, Key↔Resolve parity) — full `internal/config` package passes. - New: `SpawnCwd` decision table, and an end-to-end test that acquires an instance with a resolved root and verifies the root in status plus the child's actual cwd via `/proc//cwd`. - Existing pool/daemon test call sites updated to the `ResolvedScope` signatures; `go vet` clean for config/pool/daemon. Full suite runs in CI. ## Overlap Refs #1989: its spawn-cwd acceptance criteria 1–4 are satisfied by this change; #1989 should close as covered once this lands (its gopls live-proof criterion belongs to slice 4, #961). Slices 2/3 (#959/#960) stay blocked on this slice. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(id): comms abuse controls investigation — blocks, rate limits, per-counterparty budgets (#2032)
items.body: Investigation deliverable for #2032 (LIST 8, ID platform expansion #2056), feeding the synthesis in #2033. ## What this adds One dated record: `doc/2026-10-29T10-55-00Z_investigation_comms_abuse_controls/`. - **Control inventory** of every limiter that exists in `pkgs/id` today, with defaults and file:line: frame cap 1 MiB, world chat 50/10 s, `WorldLimits`, web save 5 s, directory-auth resend/nonce limits. - **What is absent**: no per-peer counters, no byte accounting, no block list of any kind, no `Retry-After`/`429` on any path, no config keys for abuse controls (`ServerConfig` holds only users/groups/create/policy). - **Proposed control set with defaults**, in four layers: L1 token buckets at the frame boundary (60 frames/s, burst 180, 512 KiB/s), L2 operator block list by public key / IP / topic-tag, L3 budgets (app-wide, per IP, per ID, and per-specific-counterparty overrides), L4 listener IP deny + list import. - **Composition with the accept-all-signed-objects trust model** (#2030): blocks change serving/subscribing/rendering, never acceptance of already-signed objects; refusals carry a reason class. - **Operator UX** for the "quick button", and a P0/P1/P2 shipping order answering "we don't need everything — start along this path". ## Notes - Docs-only; no code touched. No CI-relevant behaviour. - Follow-on buildable work is routed from #2032 as issues, not in this PR. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(aggregator): board in-flight lane from the orchestration section
items.body: Workstream 4: the board (/) claimed to be the curated cross-repo WIP board but the live Kaneo read is a completion record — verified today against the deployed aggregator: 64 Kaneo cards, 57 done / 7 in-review, zero in-progress / to-do (live.ts kaneoBoard keeps only in-progress/in-review/done and drops to-do as backlog, and Kaneo holds no in-progress cards). What this does (aggregator-side only; no Kaneo card is created, moved, or deleted): - live.ts board(): after the Kaneo read (+ projector link enrichment), merge synthetic in-flight entries built by the new exported helper inFlightBoardItems from the fleet feed's orchestration section — the same feed this source already reads for quota/orchestration. Per-goal linedUp tasks with status in-progress / queued / blocked become BoardItems with status 'in-flight' and source 'orchestrator' (model.ts: additive optional orchStatus/goal/blockedBy fields). - Refs: a task's explicit ref wins; otherwise refs its title carries are extracted (titleRefs: owner/repo#N / URLs, plus shorthand #N attributed to the nearest repo alias — code/opencode/openchamber/nix). The published section (2026-10-26T16:15:23Z) carries no ref fields at all, so title refs are the live path. - Dedupe: a task drops out if any of its refs already appears in a Kaneo card's links, or its title matches a Kaneo card's title; repeats inside the section emit once. Deliberately coarse (documented in code): one shared ref drops a composite entry whole. - render.ts renderBoard only: 'in-flight' is the first column, headed 'in flight — orchestrator · in flight · section (n)'; each synthetic card is badged 'orchestrator · in flight', shows its linedUp status, goal, blocked-by, and direct GitHub links for its refs. Page subtitle reframes the Kaneo columns as the curated board incl. completion history, and the in-flight lane as the being-worked-on-now answer. Verification: - New test/board-in-flight.test.ts (8 tests): status filtering, explicit + title refs, Kaneo dedupe by ref/title, intra-section dedupe, real-shape titles from the 2026-10-26 section, render lane order/header/links. Full aggregator suite: 117 pass; tsc --noEmit clean. - Real-data run (uncommitted script): real orchestration.json + the real live Kaneo board from the deployed /api/board.json → lane of 12 synthetic entries (PRs #979/#980/#759/#927, code #968 queue, nix #889/#848, incoming filings #981/#982 + oc #494/#495 + opencode #530/#529, 2 blocked, daily queues). 3 eligible tasks correctly deduped away: #944/#985 (a done Kaneo card carries both refs — PR #985 is merged), #229 and openchamber #492 (in-review Kaneo cards carry them). - Note: the current published section contains no mcpx code#958–#961 linedUp entries, so the lane cannot show them until the orchestrator republishes; the parser handles both their explicit-ref and shorthand forms (tested). Not done here: no merge, no laptop deploy, no service restart — coordinator lands and deploys. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(mcpx): decision 0004 — scope-resolved roots
items.body: Consolidates the per-project mcpx design from dezren39/nix#817 (spawn cwd = resolved scope root), #818 (`${mcpx.root}` / `${mcpx.cwd}` substitution at spawn) and #819 (initialize `rootUri`/`workspaceFolders`) into one implementable decision record: `pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0004-scope-resolved-roots.md`. What it decides beyond the three issues: - One `ResolvedScope` resolution object next to `Scope.Key` (root semantics per scope, incl. the bare-repo/submodule no-guess rule and degraded-key roots). - Plumbing path: `Registry.keyFor` → `Pool.Acquire` → instance → `dial()`; root is a pure function of the key, so restarts/redials never re-resolve. - Era identity must hash the *effective* (substituted) per-instance spawn definition. - Initialize sends `rootUri` + `workspaceFolders` for every era when a root exists; byte-identical to today when it doesn't. - codedb/codebase-memory stay deliberately `global` (multi-project inside one process); the shared index root stays a per-machine config concern. - Failure modes: vanished root = failed spawn (no silent daemon-cwd fallback); unknown `mcpx.*` placeholder = load-time config error naming server + field. Implementation is sliced into 4 issues filed from this record (linked below once filed). The nix trio stays open until the #309 re-homing pass closes them with pointers. Docs-only change; no code touched. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Added an accepted design decision describing workspace-root behavior across scopes, command working-directory precedence, and root-related variable substitution and validation. * The decision also documents initialization metadata, status and logging behavior, failure handling, and unchanged sharing and lifecycle policies. * Added the decision to the documentation index with its date and related issues.

items.title: feat(aggregator): bulk triage mode for Needs-you — multi-select batch actions (#1277)
items.body: Implements #1277 (queue task 4997): bulk triage mode for the aggregator Needs-you queues. **What changed** - `/attention` queue cards (Needs User + Needs Orchestrator, tier and session cards) carry a "Select for bulk triage" pick when the action surface is up. A card whose own controls are disabled (stale tier source) gets a disabled pick, so it can't be submitted against an unconfirmed item. - A bulk bar on the queues section: author picker, verb (acknowledge / snooze / escalate / delegate — the existing triage verbs only), the verb's payload controls, an optional reason, select-all, a live selected count, and a **review step listing every selected item + the chosen action before anything is submitted**. - New `POST /api/actions/batch`: each item is validated with the existing `validateNewAction` rules (plus the #1291/#1293 published-item checks for triage, section fetched once) and appended as **its own attributed audit entry** — never one opaque batch record — so the batch is recoverable from the entries. Response carries per-item results: failures are reported by ref with their error and append nothing, so failed items remain in Needs-you and a partial batch never silently drops work. Client tokens dedupe per item on repost, exactly like the single-action path. - The single-action path and its semantics are unchanged. **Tests** - Route tests: mixed success/failure batch (valid items recorded individually with distinct ids, invalid snooze/verb reported by ref with errors, failed refs absent from the store), per-item dedupe on repost, malformed envelopes → 400. - Render tests: picks + bulk bar render with identities, absent without. - `bun test test/actions.test.ts` — 19/19 pass. Full aggregator suite: 911 pass; the slice3 failure (`dns + sessions + pages routes serve`) and the `web-push`/`@types/bun` resolution errors are pre-existing on clean main in this worktree (no `node_modules` installed there) — verified by running slice3 with these changes stashed. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added bulk triage to the Needs User and Needs Orchestrator queues. Select eligible cards and acknowledge, snooze, escalate, or delegate them together, with an optional reason. * Review selected actions before submitting. If results are uncertain, retry without changing the reviewed actions; successful actions are cleared, while unsuccessful ones remain selected. Successful batches refresh the page. * Cards with stale sources cannot be selected for bulk actions.

items.title: fix(mcpx): lexical References scan — regex literals, bindings, no phantom declarations (#1644)
items.body: Fixes #1644 (queue task 4086, triage task 1788 CONFIRMED). `secrets.References` — the sole input to `Registry.Preflight` / `refuseScript` — was wrong in both directions. This replaces its two ad-hoc passes (a code scanner with no regex state + `declaredNames` regexing the raw source) with one lexical token pass that feeds both the binding collector and the reference finder: - **Regex literals:** the lexer has a regex-literal state (expression-position heuristic: `/` opens a regex only where a value can start — after operators, punctuation, or keywords like `return`/`typeof`/`case`; after an identifier, literal, `)`, `]`, `}` it is division). Escapes and character classes honoured, flags consumed. A reach spelled only inside a regex (`/tools.fs.read/`, `/demo.echo/`) is no longer reported. - **Lexical bindings:** declared names are collected from the token stream — `const`/`let`/`var` declarators, function names and parameters, arrow parameters (parenthesised and lone), destructured bindings (plain, renamed, nested, array), catch bindings, and the import forms the old code recognised. - **No phantom declarations:** comments, strings, template text and regex literals never produce tokens, so declaration-shaped text inside them can no longer declare a name — a real bare `demo.` reach after one is reported again. Scan stays static; nothing is evaluated. Deliberate blind spots are named in the package doc: source-global binding semantics (no block-scoped shadowing precision), a `/` directly after a value-closing `}` read as division, and method-shorthand parameters / declaration-less destructuring assignments not collected. Tests: new `TestReferencesRegexLiteralsBindingsAndPhantoms` (24 cases across the three families, plus division-after-identifier/number guards). All existing `refs_test.go` cases unchanged and passing. Laptop: `go test ./...` in pkgs/mcpx — all packages pass; gofmt/vet clean. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved detection of configured namespace references in JavaScript and TypeScript, including references in template expressions and asserted string subscripts. * Avoided false matches from comments, strings, regular expressions, and namespace names declared locally. * Improved handling of declarations, imports, parameters, and destructured bindings while keeping results unique and consistently ordered.
